title: SAR tomography detects King's Chamber, relieving chamber beams and 'sarcophagus'
place_text: King's Chamber, Great Pyramid, Giza, Egypt

tellings.quote: Again, the red is indicating a very strong vibrational signature from inside of the structure.

related.note: Both are about whether the 2020 SAR scan of the Great Pyramid picks up the King's Chamber. The story says it shows no clear signature, while this telling says it detects the chamber, the beams and the sarcophagus.

plain: A radar study of the Great Pyramid of Giza, published as a paper in 2020, is said to show the King's Chamber, the stone beams of the chambers above it that take the weight off it, and the stone box called the sarcophagus inside it. The researcher Jeffrey Drum walks Michels through the images, citing the Italian researcher Filippo Biondi. The method is SAR tomography, which uses radar signals from satellites to build up a picture of what lies inside a structure. Pointing at the colours, Drum says the red shows "a very strong vibrational signature from inside of the structure", which would mean the scan can see the pyramid's hidden insides.
